questions.question: How far may the foot brake pedal travel down when you press it hard?
options: No further than one half of the way to the floor
No further than two thirds of the way to the floor
No further than one third of the way to the floor
All the way down until it touches the floor
questions.explanation: A pedal that sinks further than that shows the system has lost pressure or the pads are worn, so the brakes may fail without warning.

questions.question: The brake fluid level in the reservoir keeps falling. What does that indicate?
options: The handbrake cables have stretched and need tightening
The system is leaking or the friction pads are worn out
The fluid has evaporated because the engine ran hot
The ABS unit has to be bled and recalibrated
questions.explanation: Brake fluid is in a sealed circuit, so a falling level means fluid is escaping or the pads have worn thin; the car belongs at a service shop.

questions.question: What does an ABS braking system do when you brake hard?
options: It shortens the braking distance on every road surface
It stops the wheels locking so the car can still be steered
It applies the handbrake as well to help the car stop
It lowers the force you need to put on the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Locked wheels lose tractive contact and the car skids out of control; ABS keeps the wheels turning so steering input still works.

questions.question: Under Icelandic traffic law, for which passengers is the driver responsible for seatbelt use?
options: For every passenger younger than 15 years of age
For every passenger younger than 12 years of age
For every passenger younger than 18 years of age
For every passenger seated in the front of the car
questions.explanation: The age of criminal responsibility in Iceland is 15, so from that age passengers answer for their own seatbelt.

questions.question: What fine can a driver expect for failing to belt a passenger under 15 years old?
options: 10 thousand ISK and one penalty point
15 thousand ISK and three penalty points
50 thousand ISK and no penalty points
15 thousand ISK and one penalty point
questions.explanation: The driver, not the child, is responsible for a passenger under 15 being belted, and answers for it with the full 15 thousand ISK fine and a penalty point.

questions.question: You are towing a wide mobile home behind your car. What does that require?
options: An extended side mirror on the driver's side only
An extra interior mirror mounted above the windscreen
Extended side mirrors fitted on both sides of the car
A rear-facing camera fitted in place of the mirrors
questions.explanation: A wide trailer hides the road behind the car on both flanks, so standard mirrors no longer give the driver a view to the rear.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a properly adjusted head restraint?
options: To cushion the head during a heavy frontal collision
To keep the occupant's head away from the side window
To limit rearward head movement and prevent whiplash
To hold the seatbelt at the correct height on the shoulder
questions.explanation: It limits how far the head travels backwards relative to the torso, protecting the cervical vertebrae; at the wrong height the injury risk rises sharply.

questions.question: Where may a child shorter than 150 cm not be seated?
options: In a front seat that has an active air bag
In any front seat of the vehicle at all
In the rear seat directly behind the driver
In a rear-facing seat in the back of the car
questions.explanation: An air bag deploys with enough force to injure or kill a small child, so it must be switched off before such a seat is used.

questions.question: In which of these situations is wearing a seatbelt not mandatory?
options: When driving at low speed on a gravel road
When driving a short errand in a residential street
When driving inside a parking garage
When the car is fitted with front and side air bags
questions.explanation: The exemptions cover reversing and driving in parking garages, gas stations, service shops and similar places, where speeds are very low.

questions.question: Your car has taken a heavy blow in a collision. What should you consider doing about the seatbelts?
options: Leave them alone, since belts are built to last the car's life
Loosen the reels so the belts run freely again
Replace them only if the air bags also deployed
Have them tested and replaced if the mechanism has gone
questions.explanation: A belt that has absorbed a strong force can have a broken mechanism; pulling it sharply should make it lock suddenly, otherwise it must be renewed.

questions.question: What is recommended before you close the deal on a used car?
options: Get a written promise from the seller that it is roadworthy
Have it inspected by a mechanic or certified service station
Book it in for a mandatory inspection within the first month
Compare its asking price against similar cars on the market
questions.explanation: An independent third party can spot wear and hidden faults that the buyer's own look over the car will miss.

questions.question: What is the first step for a car that has just been imported into Iceland?
options: It is inspected to verify it meets Icelandic requirements
It is registered and fitted with an Icelandic licence plate
It is insured with a licensed Icelandic insurance company
The import fees and taxes on the vehicle are settled
questions.explanation: Fees, insurance, registration and the plate all follow only once the car has been shown to satisfy Icelandic traffic law.

questions.question: Within what time must the transfer of a vehicle's ownership be notified?
options: Within 7 days from the date of purchase
Within 14 days from the date of purchase
Within 30 days from the date of purchase
Before the car's next mandatory inspection
questions.explanation: The register must show the real owner quickly, because insurance and inspection duties follow the registered owner.

questions.question: What does the mandatory liability insurance on a vehicle cover?
options: Losses that other people suffer in a collision you caused
Damage to your own vehicle in a collision you caused
Injury to the driver of the insured vehicle only
Damage to the windshield caused by flying stones
questions.explanation: Liability cover pays third parties for both property damage, such as another car or a lamp post, and personal injury.

questions.question: Which statement about windshield insurance in Iceland is correct?
options: It is mandatory and covers the whole cost of the repair
It is voluntary and always covers the whole cost of repair
It is mandatory for every vehicle that must be registered
It is voluntary and the owner usually pays part of the cost
questions.explanation: Only liability and accident insurance are compulsory; on a windshield claim the owner typically carries about 15 percent or a fixed extra fee.

questions.question: An insurer has paid out compensation. What is the commonest reason for it to reclaim that money from the driver?
options: The driver held no valid driving licence at the time
The driver had been racing against another vehicle
The driver caused the damage deliberately and knowingly
The driver was under the influence of alcohol or drugs
questions.explanation: All of these are grounds for a reservation of rights letter, but intoxication is by far the most frequent one, and the sums reclaimed can run to millions of ISK.

questions.question: A car's licence plate ends with the digit 0. When must it be brought for inspection?
options: In October, and at the very latest by the end of November
In December, and at the very latest by the end of February
In October, and at the very latest by the end of December
In October, with no extension of the deadline permitted
questions.explanation: The last digit names the month, and up to two further months are tolerated; the car may also be presented as early as six months ahead within the same year.

questions.question: When must a car carrying a private licence number be brought for inspection?
options: In May, in every case and without any exception
In January, unless the number ends with a numerical digit
In the month in which the car was first registered
In May, unless the number ends with a numerical digit
questions.explanation: Private plates have no digit to name a month, so May is the default; where such a plate does end in a digit, the ordinary rule applies again.

questions.question: Which piece of equipment is it mandatory to keep stored in the vehicle?
options: A small fire extinguisher
A set of snow chains
A warning triangle
A pocket flashlight
questions.explanation: A spare tyre, jack and hand tools are merely essential in practice and the winter kit is advice, but the triangle is required by law.

questions.question: Where should a fire extinguisher be kept in a private car?
options: Locked in the boot beside the spare tyre and jack
Secured, but within easy reach of the driving seat
Loose on the floor behind one of the front seats
In the engine compartment, close to the battery
questions.explanation: It has to stay put while driving yet be grabbed instantly in an emergency, which rules out both loose stowage and a locked compartment.
